speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand your symptoms better; can you tell me how long you have been experiencing the double vision, and does it worsen after physical activity? Also, have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The pattern of ptosis-like symptoms (implied by vertical gaze issues), fatigue worsened by activity and improved by rest, and specific weakness in ocular, limb, and proximal muscles is highly characteristic of this autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder. Given the severity and distribution of symptoms, I recommend a "REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibody" to confirm the diagnosis.
